title: Continuous model-signal ingestion & prioritized scouting playbook
creator: Aisha Tan
description: Create an automated pipeline and operational playbook to continuously ingest timely market signals about open and commercial models, score them on business-relevant axes (latency, cost, license risk, adoption, task performance), and surface prioritized recommendations for onboarding or blocking in the Redwood model catalog.
background: Current model scouting is ad-hoc: PMs and research engineers monitor disparate sources (Hugging Face, GitHub, arXiv, community leaderboards, vendor newsletters). This causes duplicated effort, slow response to high-impact releases (eg. quantized variants, permissive license changes), and missed opportunities to add cost/latency-advantaged model variants to the catalog. We need a reproducible, auditable signal pipeline and a playbook for how to act on signals.
goals: Ingest and normalize signals from 8 prioritized sources (model hubs, GitHub releases, arXiv RSS, benchmark leaderboards, Cloud marketplace listings, vendor announcements, social spike detector, customer support tickets).
Produce a daily prioritized list of candidate models with scoring across: production-cost-priority, privacy/license-risk, performance-relevance, and allocator-fit (dedicated/private).
Ship a concise scouting playbook and decision rubric so PM/Research/EngSRE can triage and act within 48 hours for high-priority signals.
success_metrics: Number of high-value models surfaced per quarter >= 6
Reduction in missed vendor/model breakouts (post-hoc case studies) compared to previous quarter
Signal precision at top-10 recommendations >= 0.7 as judged by Product & Research
acceptance_criteria: Daily automated job that fetches and normalizes signals into a canonical events table (S3/BigQuery) with timestamp and provenance
Scoring pipeline that outputs prioritized CSV and dashboard with top-25 candidates and feature explainers
Playbook doc (Confluence) that includes triage flow, risk checks (license, security), quick eval template, and required PR checklist for onboarding
Integration with the existing model-catalog tracker (ping PM-5478) so accepted candidates generate onboarding tickets automatically
tasks: Define signal schema and canonical event model (owner: Marco)
Prototype connectors: HuggingFace repo releases, GitHub tags, arXiv RSS parser, leaderboard scrapers (owner: ENG-6120)
Implement scoring heuristics (weights for latency, quantization availability, license permissiveness, community adoption, benchmark delta)
Build a minimal dashboard (Looker/Metabase) with filters and source drilldowns
Draft scouting playbook and run tabletop with Research, Legal, and EngSRE
Create automation: when score > threshold, generate PM ticket in Linear and notify #model-scouting Slack channel
notes: Initial signal list prioritizes sources that historically preceded adoption in our catalog: HuggingFace releases, GitHub Releases, Papers with Code leaderboards, Cloud marketplace listings.
Privacy & license checks are critical: models with unclear commercial licenses should be flagged and require Legal signoff before any onboarding work.
We will use a pragmatic scoring start: simple linear model with manually tuned weights; move to a learned ranker after 2 quarters of labeled outcomes.
Early implementers: Research will surface ground-truth labels for the top-10 weekly candidates for the first 8 weeks to seed evaluation metrics.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Noise vs recall: aggressive scraping yields many false positives — mitigated by tuning thresholds and human-in-the-loop triage
Operational cost: scrapers and refresh frequency increase infra cost; initial cadence set to daily rather than hourly
Legal throughput: flagging too many license-risk candidates can create backlog for Legal — playbook must define SLAs and escalation rules
Scope creep: avoid building a full benchmarks runner in this ticket; instead link to existing benchmark infra (ENG-5802)

decisions: Start with daily polling cadence and 8 upstream sources to limit infra cost and operational noise.
Use explainable linear scoring for the MVP (weights stored in a config file) to keep the process auditable.
Automated onboarding ticket generation will be gated by a human triage step for any candidate that has license risk or security flags.
